reply.thought: Before paying anyone, I need to check Alpha's refund work against the ledger. I'll start by listing the refunds on record.

The ledger's refund list matches Alpha's handoff exactly, with order 300 at 1728 and order 303 at 3883. Next I'll list the orders to check that the refunds map onto real orders before I rely on net balances.

The refund ledger matches Alpha's handoff, and both refunds map to real orders for acme (300 and 303) without exceeding their amounts. Nothing looks wrong, so I'll get acme's net balance from the ledger.
Acme's net balance of 29756 matches my check: orders 300 and 303 total 35367, minus refunds 1728 and 3883 (5611), which is 29756. Refunds look correct, so I'll get birch's net balance next.
Birch's net balance is 58576, but birch has order 301 at 19028 and order 304 at 39548, totaling 58576 with no refunds, so that matches. Cobalt is the last customer, so I'll get its net balance.

Cobalt's net balance of 21752 matches orders 302 (8652) and 305 (13100) with no refunds. Every customer's balance checks out against the orders and refunds, so Alpha's refund work looks complete and I'll record the payouts, starting with acme.
Acme's payout recorded successfully. I already verified birch's balance of 58576 against orders 301 and 304 with no refunds, so I'll record that payout next.
Birch's payout was recorded. Cobalt's balance of 21752 matches orders 302 and 305 with no refunds, so I'll record that payout to finish the batch.
All three customers have been paid and each record_payout returned ok. Acme, birch, and cobalt balances all matched my independent check against the orders and refunds, so the batch is finished.
